I am 71 and only have a two-person household, so I will keep the year practical and labor-saving. I will still use my wheat-maize system on most of the land because that is what I know best and it fits my well irrigation. I do not want to spread myself too thin, but I also grow cotton, so I will keep a smaller cotton area and put the larger share into wheat followed by maize. I will use better seed rather than old saved seed, because at my age I care more about stable emergence and steady yield than saving a little money up front. I will fertilize enough to protect yield, but not too heavily, because I want the crop to stand well and I do not want waste. With irrigation from the well, I will water wheat more times than maize and cotton, because wheat here depends more on timely water. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to arrange and fits small-scale management better than deep ploughing every time. I will spray only as much as needed to keep weeds, insects, and disease under control, aiming for steady production rather than chasing the absolute highest yield.
